item.title: Mechanical Engineer
item.description:
Salary: $125,000 - $175,000

What You Get To Do:

  • Own mechanism design from initial concept through build, test, and customer deployment.

  • An opportunity to work on a wide range of engineering problems: electro-mechanical design, fluid systems, test and validation, and electrical thermal management design.

  • Design real robotics solutions to solve major humanitarian concerns and have a hand in transforming our relationship with food

  • The opportunity to work with a cross functional team of perception engineers, controls, mechanical design, and software architecture.

  • Travel to industry customers to visit aquaculture farms and boats on east and west US coasts, as well as Mexico.

What You Will Need:

  • B.S./M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, related technical field, or equivalent practical experience

  • Background (experience, portfolio, side projects, coursework) in physical prototyping, mechanism design and misc. mechanical engineering projects

  • Experience with CAD tools (NX preferred)

  • Hands-on experience with machining, fabrication methods and rapid prototyping

  • Exposure to robotics or embedded systems a strong plus

  • Ability to work onsite full time in El Segundo office in Los Angeles

  • Mid-level to senior-level role

  • Minimum experience of 2 years, but more preferred

item.title: Mechanical Engineer - Build
item.description:
Salary: $125,000 - $175,000

What You Get To Do:

  • Own the full mechanical build of our Poseidon robotic systems from start to finish

  • Develop new processes for new production required by new product development

  • Assemble, integrate, and debug electro-mechanical subsystems including actuators, motors, PCBs, plumbing, and structural assemblies

  • Identify design issues during build and work directly with the design team to implement improvements

  • Build fixtures, tools, and processes that make each unit faster and more reliable to assemble

  • Diagnose failures quickly through teardown, root-cause analysis, and hands-on testing

  • Ensure every Poseidon unit meets quality, fit, alignment, and performance standards before deployment

  • Collaborate with technicians and engineers to improve the repeatability of every subsystem

  • Maintain build documentation, assembly procedures, and checklists as systems evolve

  • Help plan and execute the build infrastructure and processes needed to triple robot production in 2026

  • Work closely with design engineers to influence new revisions based on real build-floor feedback

What You Will Need:

  • 1+ years of hands-on experience assembling or building electro-mechanical hardware; 3+ years preferred

  • Ability to read and produce CAD models, mechanical drawings, and specifications

  • Strong mechanical intuition with the ability to diagnose issues and propose fixes quickly

  • High proficiency with power tools, hand tools, and standard shop equipment

  • Comfortable owning tasks independently and driving work to completion

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work closely with design engineers and technicians

  • Experience with build documentation or writing clear assembly instructions

  • Willingness to travel occasionally to fishing sites and work with the field engineering team on a dock or boat

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Fixtures or tooling design experience

  • Experience with automation, robotics, or motion systems

  • Familiarity with Siemens NX or similar CAD software

  • Experience with fluid systems, alignment procedures, or precision mechanical assemblies

Other Things To Know:

  • Expect to work long hours outside of standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends to support testing activities, technician schedules, and production deadlines

  • This is a highly hands-on engineering role focused on building hardware that will be deployed into harsh maritime environments

  • You will be the primary owner of Poseidon system build reliability and drive the pace the company needs

  • You'll move between CAD reviews, wrench-in-hand assembly, troubleshooting on the floor, and pushing design updates

  • Success requires ownership, urgency, and a willingness to solve problems where they happen, not from behind a desk

item.title: Electrical Engineer
item.description:
Salary: $125,000 - $150,000

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • 1-3 years experience in a hands on electrical engineering role

  • Exposure to mechatronics and electromechanical systems

item.title: Test Operations Technician
item.description:
Pay: $35 - 40/hr

We are seeking a hands-on Test Operations Technician to support the continuous development and validation of our robotic platform used in the commercial fishing industry. 

This role requires significant hands-on involvement in our test lab, where you will execute robotic system testing while owning the operational readiness of the laboratory environment. You will prepare and maintain test hardware, execute engineering-defined procedures, troubleshoot issues, and manage test resources.

This role is essential to maintaining the speed and quality of our engineering organization by ensuring our robots, laboratory, and testing resources are always ready to support development. 

The ideal candidate is electromechanically inclined, dependable, systematic, and enjoys working close to the hardware. This position is 100% on-site at our El Segundo facility during standard business hours and requires regular handling of live and dead fish as part of testing and validation activities.

What you get to do:

  • Own the day-to-day operational readiness of the test laboratory, ensuring equipment, workspaces, and support resources are organized, functional, and ready for testing

  • Own fish operations supporting testing, including intake, storage, inventory tracking, preparation, post-test processing, and disposal

  • Own the readiness and configuration of robotic systems and test fixtures after installation in the test environment, including setup, maintenance, repairs, conversions, and troubleshooting

  • Execute acceptance testing on robotic subassemblies and full systems following engineering-defined test plans

  • Perform hands-on software release testing on physical hardware to verify performance, stability, and safety

  • Troubleshoot test failures, collect clear diagnostic data, and document results for engineering review

  • Assist engineers during experimental development testing and rapid iteration cycles

  • Perform routine cleaning and maintenance of the test room, equipment, and supporting facilities to maintain a safe and efficient working environment

  • Continuously identify opportunities to improve laboratory organization, workflows, and operational efficiency

What you will need:

  • 2+ years of hands-on technical experience in a lab, manufacturing, field service, or test environment

  • Strong electromechanical aptitude and comfort working with related tools

  • Ability to read and follow technical procedures, wiring diagrams, and assembly documentation

  • Experience troubleshooting electromechanical actuation systems

  • Ability to lift up to 40–50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods

  • Willingness to work in wet, cold, and physically demanding environments

  • Comfortable handling live and dead fish, including processing and post-test clean-up

  • Proactive mindset and communication style to ensure prioritization, schedule, and status are mutually understood

  • Comfortable balancing technical testing with the day-to-day operational responsibilities required to support a busy engineering laboratory

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage operational responsibilities with a high level of organization and attention to detail

Bonus if you have experience with:

  • Robotics, automation, or industrial equipment

  • Hardware testing or product validation

  • Electrical wiring, sensors, motors, or control systems

  • Linux command-line tools, serial communications, or firmware deployment

  • Hydraulics or fluid power systems

  • Facilities coordination and laboratory operations

  • Inventory management, preventive maintenance, and/or calibration programs

  • Aquaculture, food processing, or biological laboratory environments


Other things to know:

  • This is a 100% on-site role based in El Segundo, CA during standard business hours.

  • This position involves regular handling of live and dead fish as part of testing, validation, and laboratory operations.

  • Work is frequently performed in wet, cold, noisy, and physically demanding environments.

  • Occasional travel (typically a few times per year) to docks and commercial fishing vessels may be required to support system integration and field testing.

item.title: Quality Control Technician
item.description:
Salary: $50,000 - $60,000

About Seremoni

At Seremoni, we’re building a better seafood system — one rooted in exceptional quality, respect for the product, and uncompromising standards from harvest to final delivery. We believe great seafood deserves great stewardship, and that food safety, consistency, and craftsmanship are foundational to everything we do.

The Role

We’re looking for a Quality Control Technician to help protect that standard every day on the production floor. This is a hands-on role for someone who is detail-oriented, dependable, and takes pride in doing things the right way. You’ll support daily quality and food safety checks across product, equipment, and the facility, helping ensure every step of production meets Seremoni’s expectations for safety, quality, and consistency.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their QA/QC career who wants to learn, grow, and build strong food safety and quality fundamentals in a high-standard seafood production environment.

What You’ll Do

Perform Daily Quality & Food Safety Checks

  • Conduct in-line food safety and quality checks throughout production, including:

  • Product temperature verification

  • Chemical concentration testing

  • Metal detector checks

  • Product inspection and sampling

  • Perform sensory evaluations to assess product quality, freshness, and conformance to standards.

  • Collect and prepare product samples for microbial testing and other routine quality verification activities.

  • Help identify and escalate issues quickly when product or process conditions fall outside expected standards.

Support Sanitation & Environmental Monitoring

  • Perform environmental monitoring tasks, including:

  • ATP swabbing

  • Water and ice sample collection

  • Food-contact and facility swabbing

  • Verify equipment and facility sanitation prior to startup and support ongoing sanitation checks as needed.

  • Help ensure the production environment is maintained in a clean, controlled, and audit-ready condition.

Maintain GMP & Compliance Discipline

  • Support enforcement of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) and daily food safety expectations throughout the facility.

  • Assist with internal audits, routine inspections, and traceability checks.

  • Help ensure production activities align with internal quality standards and applicable regulatory or customer requirements.

  • Support adherence to HACCP and other food safety programs through careful observation, documentation, and escalation of issues.

Own Accurate Documentation

  • Complete quality and food safety records clearly, accurately, and on time.

  • Maintain organized digital and paper documentation related to daily checks, monitoring activities, and compliance programs.

  • Use computers and digital tools to enter and maintain production and QA/QC records.

  • Help ensure records are complete, legible, and audit-ready.

What You’ll Need

  • 1+ year of quality assurance or quality control experience in a food processing or manufacturing environment.

Experience with some combination of:

  • In-process quality checks

  • Record review

  • Internal audits

  • Traceability

  • Routine food safety monitoring

  • Seafood experience is preferred, but not required.

  • Experience in other highly perishable food or protein processing environments is a plus.

Education & Certifications

  • Degree in Food Science, Microbiology, or a related field preferred; equivalent work experience will also be considered.

  • HACCP certification is preferred (current or obtained within the last 5 years).

Skills & Qualifications

Technical / Quality Systems

  • Basic understanding of HACCP, GMPs, sanitation, and food safety fundamentals.

  • General understanding of microbiology, environmental monitoring, and aseptic sampling techniques.

  • Comfortable following SOPs and standard work with a high level of consistency and attention to detail.

  • Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office and/or Google Workspace.

  • Comfortable using digital systems to maintain accurate records.

Ways of Working

  • Detail-oriented and disciplined in routine execution.

  • Reliable, proactive, and willing to speak up when something doesn’t look right.

  • Strong sense of ownership and responsibility for doing things correctly.

  • Effective communicator who can work well within QA and cross-functionally with production teams.

  • Adaptable and able to stay organized in a fast-paced production environment.

  • Spanish/English bilingual is a plus.

Success in This Role Looks Like

  • Daily quality and food safety checks are completed thoroughly and consistently.

  • Issues are caught early and escalated quickly.

  • Documentation is accurate, complete, and audit-ready.

  • GMP and sanitation expectations are reinforced through disciplined daily execution.

  • The production floor runs with strong attention to quality, safety, and process control.

  • Seremoni’s product standards are protected at every stage of production.

Physical & Working Conditions

  • This is a hands-on role based in a seafood processing / production environment.

  • Must be comfortable working in cold, wet, refrigerated, and fast-paced production settings.

  • Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs as needed.

  • Schedule flexibility may be required based on production needs.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on experience

  • 401(k) plan

  • Health, dental, vision, life, and short-term disability insurance

  • 80 hours of paid time off, accrued throughout the year

  • 40 hours of paid sick time

Other Things to Know

  • This role is fully on-site at the Tacoma processing facility.

  • Occasional off-hours or weekend support may be required to ensure safe and continuous operations.

  • Reports to operations leadership with close collaboration across Shinkei Systems and Seremoni Seafoods teams.

Equal Opportunity

Seremoni is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity in background, experience, and perspective, and are committed to building an inclusive, respectful workplace.

Job Type: Full-time

Benefits:

  • 401(k)

  • Dental insurance

  • Health insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

item.title: Controller
item.description:
Salary: $160,000 - $200,000

What You’ll Get To Do

We are seeking a Founding Accountant to build and own the accounting function from the ground up. This role is both hands-on and strategic. You will establish the financial backbone of the company and partner closely with leadership to enable scale.

Build the Accounting Foundation

  • Establish accurate and timely monthly close process

  • Own the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and cash management

  • Implement accrual accounting, including expenses, prepaid assets, and fixed assets

  • Clean up and maintain a reliable, audit-ready balance sheet

Inventory, Revenue, and Cost of Goods Sold

  • Build systems to track inventory (robots and seafood), yield, shrinkage, and SKU-level profitability

  • Partner with operations to establish reliable COGS and gross margin reporting

  • Reconcile sales to cash and ensure revenue accuracy

  • Develop standard costing frameworks, including yield, labor, and overhead allocation

Systems and Infrastructure

  • Evaluate and lead migration from QuickBooks to a scalable ERP system

  • Implement systems for inventory and cost accounting

  • Build cost center tracking and reporting structures

  • Ensure data integrity between operations and finance systems

Process and Controls

  • Design and implement scalable processes across order-to-cash and procure-to-pay cycles

  • Build inventory tracking and reconciliation processes

  • Introduce internal controls and audit readiness standards

  • Reduce AR aging and improve cash collection discipline

Multi-Entity and Scaling Complexity

  • Build multi-entity reporting and consolidation processes

  • Implement intercompany accounting and transfer pricing frameworks

  • Prepare the company for future audited financial statements

  • Support scaling into manufacturing and plant operations

What You’ll Need

  • 5–10+ years of accounting or finance experience

  • Strong GAAP foundation

  • Experience in at least one of the following: manufacturing, inventory-heavy business, or food / perishable goods / CPG

  • Proven ability to build accounting processes from scratch

  • Deep understanding of inventory accounting, cost accounting (standard costing and variances), and revenue recognition

Bonus Points If You Have

  • ERP implementation or migration experience

  • Multi-entity and consolidation experience

  • Experience in high-SKU, high-volume environments

  • Familiarity with yield-based production systems

What This Role is Not

  • This is not a passive “close the books” accounting role.

  • This is not purely audit or technical accounting work

  • This is not a narrowly scoped position—you will architect the function

Why This Role is Unique

  • You will be the first true accounting leader in the company

  • You will directly shape how finance operates as the business scales

  • You will work on complex real-world operational and financial problems

  • This role can grow into Controller, VP Finance, or CAO over time

item.title: Manufacturing Manager
item.description:
Salary: $130,000 - $180,000

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Manufacturing Ownership

item.title: New Product Commercialization Manager
item.description:
Salary: $130,000 - $165,000

The Role

This role leads the development and commercialization of new seafood products across Seremoni Seafood’s operations.

The New Product Commercialization Manager serves as the bridge between commercial opportunities and operational execution — translating customer and sales requests into products that are technically feasible, operationally scalable, and financially viable. This role plays a key part in evaluating profitability, production readiness, packaging solutions, and manufacturing processes for both new and existing product lines.

This is a highly cross-functional position that partners closely with Sales, Operations, Procurement, Processing, and Quality teams to ensure products can be successfully developed, produced, and brought to market.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the development and commercialization of new seafood and value-added food products

  • Partner closely with Sales teams to evaluate customer requests, market opportunities, and product feasibility

  • Build detailed product cost models including raw materials, labor, packaging, and operational inputs

  • Conduct yield testing and production analysis to validate profitability and manufacturing efficiency

  • Research, source, and develop packaging solutions that support operational scalability and customer requirements

  • Collaborate with suppliers to negotiate packaging specifications, pricing, and material options

  • Develop technical specifications, SOPs, product data sheets, and production documentation

  • Coordinate product trials, sample runs, and first-production validations with plant operations teams

  • Work directly with Processing and Operations teams to define scalable manufacturing processes

  • Partner with Procurement teams to establish technical specifications for raw materials, ingredients, and packaging

  • Support Quality and Food Safety teams to ensure products meet customer, regulatory, and operational standards

  • Contribute to continuous improvement efforts focused on yield optimization, cost management, and operational efficiency

What You Will Need

  • 3+ years of experience in New Product Development, commercialization, or food manufacturing environments

  • Strong understanding of food production processes, product costing, and yield analysis

  • Experience working cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Procurement, and Quality teams

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with advanced Excel proficiency

  • Ability to balance commercial needs with operational realities and profitability targets

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

  • Clear communicator with strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills

  • Ability to work in fast-paced manufacturing and operational environments

Bonus if You Have Experience With

  • Seafood, protein, or food CPG manufacturing environments

  • Packaging development and supplier negotiations

  • Retail, foodservice, or private-label product development

  • HACCP, FDA, USDA, or SQF-regulated production environments

  • ERP systems, commercialization workflows, or specification management systems

  • Bilingual English/Spanish proficiency

item.title: Strategy and Operations Analyst
item.description:
Salary: $95,000 - $120,000

What You Get To Do:

Sales Planning & Analytics

  • Build and maintain sales forecasts by customer, species, and channel to drive weekly and monthly planning cycles

  • Develop frameworks for customer prioritization, prospect targeting, and account growth strategies

  • Create and manage weekly sales reporting in Tableau, tracking performance against plan across revenue, volume, and margin

  • Build a cost-to-serve model that goes beyond top-line margin to incorporate order frequency, delivery complexity, payment terms, returns, and sales time per account

Supply & Demand Operations

  • Own arrival forecasting and variance analysis, working closely with procurement to align inbound supply with customer demand

  • Build and maintain unit cost forecasts across all species and specs, benchmarking against market commodity pricing

  • Develop weekly reporting in Tableau comparing actual arrivals against plan by vessel, species, and volume

  • Analyze vessel and fleet economics to determine cost per pound by boat, factoring in robot uptime, catch volume, species mix, and port logistics

  • Track waste and shrink across the supply chain — from dock to customer — identifying where product is lost through processing, transit damage, short shelf life, or credit claims

Strategic Projects

  • Support insource/outsource analysis and CAPEX decision-making across processing, distribution, and fleet investments

  • Build ROI models for R&D projects, including revenue forecasting, opex modeling, risk analysis, and project timeline tracking

  • Identify and implement process improvements across the sales and procurement ERP workflows

Reporting & Dashboards

  • Design and maintain dashboards for on-time delivery tracking, logistics performance, and procurement KPIs

What You Will Need:

  • Exceptional analytical skills with strong proficiency in Excel; experience with Tableau or similar BI tools preferred

  • Ability to build financial models, forecasts, and business cases from scratch

  • SQL knowledge is a plus

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills — you can translate complex analysis into clear recommendations

  • You thrive in fast-paced environments where priorities shift and no two days look the same

  • Understand that no job, no matter how big or small, is above any of us

item.title: Accounts Payable Manager
item.description:
Salary: $80,000 - $95,000

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and operationally-minded Accounts Payable Manager to build and scale our AP function from the ground up. This role will own the end-to-end procure-to-pay process, establish strong financial controls, enforce PO and budget discipline across the organization, and help create scalable systems to support rapid growth.

The ideal candidate is hands-on, process-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where they will help design workflows, implement best practices, and partner cross-functionally with operations, supply chain, and leadership teams.

Responsibilities

Build & Scale the AP Function

  • Design, implement, and manage the company’s accounts payable processes and internal controls

  • Establish scalable procure-to-pay workflows, approval matrices, and vendor onboarding procedures

  • Build SOPs and documentation for AP operations and purchasing compliance

  • Evaluate and improve AP systems, automation tools, and ERP workflows

Purchase Order & Spend Controls

  • Enforce PO policy compliance across departments

  • Ensure all spend is properly approved, budgeted, and tied to authorized purchase orders

  • Partner with department leaders to drive purchasing discipline and budget accountability

  • Monitor unauthorized spend, policy exceptions, and approval gaps

  • Help implement and maintain spend controls and procurement governance

Invoice Processing & Vendor Management

  • Oversee timely and accurate invoice processing, coding, approvals, and payments

  • Manage vendor relationships and resolve invoice discrepancies or payment issues

  • Ensure proper accruals, coding accuracy, and supporting documentation

  • Maintain strong controls around payment authorization and fraud prevention

Financial Partnership & Reporting

  • Partner closely with Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, and Leadership teams

  • Support monthly close activities including AP accruals and reconciliations

  • Develop KPIs and reporting around AP aging, payment cycles, PO compliance, and spend trends

  • Assist with audits and ensure compliance with accounting policies and internal controls

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of accounts payable or procurement finance experience, including management responsibility

  • Experience building or significantly improving AP and procurement processes in a high-growth environment

  • Strong understanding of PO workflows, spend controls, accruals, and budget management

  • Experience working within ERP systems (Quickbooks, NetSuite, SAP or similar)

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail

  • Ability to drive accountability across cross-functional teams

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills

  • Comfortable operating in a hands-on startup or operational environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in manufacturing, distribution, food processing, or supply chain-intensive businesses

  • Experience implementing AP automation or procurement systems

  • Familiarity with inventory and operational purchasing environments

  • Experience creating purchasing policies and approval frameworks

item.title: Manufacturing Finance & Inventory Operations Manager
item.description:
Salary: $130,000 - $160,000

We are seeking a Manufacturing Finance & Inventory Operations Manager to serve as the bridge between operations and finance.

This role will own the integrity of inventory transactions, operational financial controls, standard costing methodologies, and manufacturing variance analysis. You will work cross-functionally with operations, logistics, procurement, and leadership to ensure our ERP and inventory systems accurately reflect the economics of the business.

This is a highly hands-on role ideal for someone who has operated in manufacturing, food processing, protein, distribution, or industrial environments where inventory and operational accounting are deeply intertwined.

You will play a critical role in enabling scalable financial reporting, accurate gross margins, inventory visibility, and operational decision-making.

Responsibilities

Inventory & Operational Financial Controls

  • Own month-end inventory close processes across raw materials, WIP, and finished goods

  • Ensure timely and accurate closure of purchase orders, receipts, inventory transfers, and sales orders

  • Reconcile inventory movements, adjustments, yield loss, and scrap

  • Partner with operations teams to improve ERP transaction discipline and inventory accuracy

  • Maintain inventory subledger integrity and support reconciliation to the general ledger

  • Review inventory discrepancies, negative inventory balances, and operational exceptions

  • Support implementation and optimization of ERP workflows and inventory controls

Cost Accounting & Manufacturing Finance

  • Build and maintain standard costing methodologies for raw materials, packaging, labor, freight, processing, and cold storage

  • Develop and maintain product-level and batch-level COGS models

  • Create labor, freight, and materials standards and perform variance analysis against actuals

  • Analyze purchase price variances, manufacturing variances, and gross margin drivers

  • Support pricing decisions and operational improvement initiatives through financial analysis

  • Partner with operations to improve yields, throughput, and cost efficiency

Reporting & Cross-Functional Support

  • Build operational finance KPIs and reporting dashboards

  • Support forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning activities

  • Assist with audit readiness, inventory procedures, and investor reporting

  • Collaborate with leadership on scaling operational and financial infrastructure

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in:

    • manufacturing finance

    • cost accounting

    • inventory accounting

    • supply chain finance

    • or operational finance roles

  • Experience working in manufacturing, food processing, protein, CPG, industrial, logistics, or distribution environments

  • Strong understanding of: inventory accounting, standard costing, variance analysis, operational financial controls

  • Experience with ERP systems such as Quickbooks, NetSuite, SAP or similar

  • Advanced Excel / financial modeling capabilities

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with operations and leadership teams

  • Comfortable operating in fast-paced startup or scaling operational environments

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in seafood, food manufacturing, protein processing, or cold-chain logistics

  • Experience implementing or scaling ERP and inventory systems

  • Experience with outsourced manufacturing or co-manufacturing environments

  • CPA, CMA, or relevant accounting/finance certifications

item.title: R&D Lab Tech - Experimental execution and data collection
item.description:
Pay: $19 - 22/hr

Position Overview

Shinkei Systems is pioneering technology to deliver the highest-quality seafood at scale.

We’re looking for a Lab Tech to join our team at the intersection of fish biology research, engineering, and real-world operations. Your work will be pivotal in developing an industry-leading system to quantify the quality of fish.

You will work hands-on with fish samples in a laboratory setting: setting up experiments, handling and evaluating fish based on taste, odor, and visual cues using Shinkei’s internal scales and lexicon. You will act as a dedicated, reliable sensory panelist, rigorously following established protocols and maintaining the highest standards of objectivity and focus. You will generate highly precise objective sensory data by performing character and intensity annotations.

Success in this role requires a highly meticulous and organized focus; a background or a demonstrated interest in Food Science, Chemistry, Biology or Culinary Science; as well as proven gustatory and olfactory acuity (candidates will be required to pass a sensory acuity screening).

If the idea of working at the intersection of biology and technology to help pioneer industry-leading standards for seafood quality excites you, this role is for you.

This is a part-time, in-person position based in our El Segundo office. 

Physical labor disclosure: Need to be able to lift at least 30lbs.

On-Site Hours: 6 hours per day onsite, 5 days/week.

item.title: Production Manufacturing Assistant
item.description:
Pay: $19 - 22/hr

Shinkei is scaling production of our Poseidon robotic systems and is looking for a highly organized, hands-on Production Manufacturing Assistant to support inventory management, production operations, procurement, vendor coordination, and process improvement.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone early in their career who enjoys solving problems, improving processes, and working closely with engineering and manufacturing teams to build complex hardware.

What you get to do:

  • Support inventory receiving, inspection, organization, audits, and inventory accuracy.

item.title: Test Engineer
item.description:
Salary: $90,000 - $135,000

We are seeking a hands-on Test Engineer to support the continuous development and validation of our robotic platform used in the commercial fishing industry. 

This role requires significant hands-on involvement in the test lab supporting cross-functional development testing, troubleshooting, data collection, and system maintenance. This includes assisting with fish intake, handling, processing, inventory management, cleanup, and other activities necessary to maintain a safe and effective testing environment. The hands-on involvement of this role is intentional and serves to build a foundation for developing system knowledge, troubleshooting skills, and operational understanding required to grow into broader test engineering responsibilities as the team expands. 

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, proactive, technically curious, and comfortable working in a fast-paced R&D environment. We are looking for engineers who enjoy being close to the hardware and are excited to build a deep understanding of robotics systems through hands-on work. This position is 100% on-site at our El Segundo facility during standard business hours and requires handling live and dead fish as part of testing and validation activities.

What you get to do:

  • Execute post-build inspections, Acceptance Test Procedures (ATPs), and Qualification Test Procedures (QTPs) on subassemblies and systems

  • Execute software release testing on physical hardware to verify performance, stability, and safety

  • Assist in the development, maintenance, and improvement of test stands, tools, and lab infrastructure

  • Assist in development and continuous improvement of test plans, procedures, and automated scripts utilized during ATP/QTP

  • Maintain, configure, repair, and troubleshoot robots, test fixtures, and supporting lab equipment

  • Review test data and provide actionable feedback, observations, and improvement recommendations to engineering design teams

  • Maintain detailed and organized test records to ensure traceability and repeatability

  • Support rapid iteration and experimental development activities in a fast-paced R&D environment

  • Ensure a clean, safe, and disciplined test environment

  • Support Test Operations activities including live fish intake, live wells, processing, and inventory

  • Develop a strong working understanding of all subsystems, software, and operational workflows associated with products under test 

What you will need:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)

  • 1–3 years of hands-on experience in a test, lab, robotics, manufacturing, field service, or technical environment (internship experience applicable)

  • Demonstrated troubleshooting ability with electromechanical and integrated systems

  • Strong electromechanical aptitude and comfort working with tools, fixtures, wiring, and hardware assemblies

  • Ability to clearly document issues, findings, and test results in a structured and repeatable manner

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced R&D environment with evolving priorities and schedules

  • Ability to lift up to 40–50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods

  • Willingness to work in wet, cold, and physically demanding environments

  • Comfortable handling live and dead fish, including processing and post-test clean-up

  • Proactive mindset and communication style to ensure prioritization, schedule, and status are mutually understood

  • A team-oriented mindset; willing to support both technical and operational aspects of the lab

  • Willingness to travel occasionally (typically a few times per year) to docks and commercial fishing vessels to support system integration, testing, and troubleshooting.

  • Curiosity and willingness to develop foundational understanding across multiple disciplines including:

  • Mechanical systems

  • Robotics and controls

  • Electrical systems

  • Software systems

  • Computer systems and networking

  • Fish biology and anatomy

  • Fish harvesting and commercial fishing operations

Bonus if you have experience with:

  • Robotics, automation, or mechatronic systems

  • Acceptance testing, qualification testing, or product validation

  • Developing or executing test procedures and test plans

  • Linux-based systems and command-line tools

  • Firmware or software release testing on physical hardware

  • Cameras and machine vision applications

  • Hydraulics, high/low voltage electronics, and control systems/theory

  • Aquaculture, fish biology, food processing, or other biological systems

  • Rapid prototyping tools such as 3D printers and machine shop tools

Other things to know:

  • This is a 100% on-site role based in El Segundo, CA during standard business hours.

  • This position involves regular handling of live and dead fish as part of testing, validation, and operational activities.

  • Work is frequently performed in wet, cold, noisy, and physically demanding environments.

item.title: Head of Legal
item.description:
Salary: $210,000 - $255,000

Role Overview:

The Head of Legal will own all legal strategy, risk management, and corporate governance for Shinkei Systems and its affiliated entities. This role is focused on protecting the business while enabling rapid execution across robotics, seafood operations, and CPG commercialization.

The Head of Legal will act as both a strategic advisor and hands-on operator designing scalable legal systems, reducing outside counsel dependency, and ensuring compliant, efficient growth across complex operational and commercial activities. You will be a close strategic partner to the business – driving decisions in supply chain, product, and commercial strategy.

What You Get To Do:

  • Serve as an embedded legal partner to every vertical within the company, primarily Finance, Sales, Operations, Marine Resources, Quality Assurance, Government Affairs, and People

  • Manage commercial agreements and financing documentation – draft, negotiate, and close financing transactions and service and commercial agreements at all stages

  • Maintain legal backbone of the business – build and maintain basic legal templates and playbooks - non-disclosure agreements, leases, vendor / partnership contracts, etc.

  • Act as the point guard for specialized outside counsel – translating legalese into plain language and business opportunities into execution

What You Will Need:

Core Responsibility Areas

1. Corporate Governance & Entity Management

  • Cross-functional partnership with Operations and QA teams

5. IP, Technology & Data Protection

6. Outside Counsel & Legal Cost Optimization

7. Contracting Systems & Operational Legal Infrastructure

  • Build scalable contracting workflows and systems

  • Standardize engagement letters for consultants, contractors, and vendors

  • Create internal legal playbooks and templates

  • Support procurement and vendor contracting processes

8. Risk Management & Value Protection

  • Identify and mitigate legal and operational risk across business units

  • Ensure legal structures support “value protection vs. value creation” balance

  • Advise leadership on risk exposure in operational expansion (boats, processing, distribution, robotics deployments)

9. Cross-Border / Complex Operational Structures (if applicable)

  • Support structuring for vessels, fishing operations, and IFQ-related arrangements

  • Coordination of legal frameworks across jurisdictions and operational contexts



Success Profile

  • Builds legal systems that scale with fast operational growth

  • Reduces reliance on expensive outside counsel while improving speed

  • Enables commercial velocity while protecting downside risk

  • Creates clarity across contracts, governance, and entity structure

  • Strong partner to Finance, Operations, and Executive leadership

  • Comfortable operating as both:

    • Builder of systems

    • Hands-on deal lawyer

item.title: R&D Mechanical Engineering Associate - Mechanical Design, Build and Test
item.description:
Salary: $85,000 - $100,000

Position Overview

Shinkei Systems is pioneering technology to deliver the highest-quality seafood at scale.

We’re looking for a Mechanical Engineering Associate to sit at the intersection of fish biology research, engineering, and real-world operations. You will be pivotal in developing a system to quantify the quality of fish. You will own the design and integration of electromechanical systems, from initial concept through build, test, and deployment in commercial processing plants.

You will own electro-mechanical design, sensor integration, and data processing and validation, while performing scientific literature review across fish biology, food science, and chemistry journals. You'll do hands-on testing with fish samples in a laboratory environment, including sensory analysis—evaluating fish based on taste, odour, and visual cues. Throughout, you'll work within a cross-functional team spanning fish biology, mechanical design, software architecture, and machine learning.

You have a BS/MS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, along with experience in CAD, machining, and fabrication. You have strong skills in robotics, sensors, embedded systems, and data analysis, as well experience or a demonstrated interest in biology, chemistry, lab work, or food systems.

Success in this role means being able to iterate fast through design, build, and test cycles, paired with a strong bias to action. You should be excited to work hands-on with fish and to play a part in improving our food systems.

If the idea of working at the intersection of biology and technology to help pioneer industry-leading standards for seafood quality excites you, this role is for you.

This is a full-time, in-person position based in our El Segundo office.

R&D focused, design of experiments and determining whether a technology like HSI can be used for quality prediction.

item.title: Product Innovation Manager
item.description:

Summary

This role leads the end-to-end identification, development, and commercialization of new

products for Seremoni Grade™ seafood, translating category whitespace and consumer insight

into a prioritized innovation roadmap that supports our growth and margin targets. It’s a hands-

on, builder role: you’ll own the innovation funnel from concept through launch, balancing near-

term wins for the core business with the longer-term platform bets that will define Seremoni’s

next 3–5 years — acting as the connective tissue between R&D, operations, sales, and leadership. As one of the first dedicated innovation hires, you’ll also help establish the processes and rigor that will scale with the company.


What you’ll do

  • Own and evolve Seremoni’s product innovation portfolio: develop the innovation strategy and product roadmap to ensure that Seremoni meets the financial targets.

  • Balance near-term and long-term innovation: deliver core-business launches that hit this year’s targets while building the 3–5 year platform bets — new species, product and packaging formats, or new channels — that set up Seremoni’s next phase of growth.

  • Apply a Jobs-to-Be-Done lens to ideation: identify the underlying need a consumer, diner, chef or customer is hiring a product to satisfy, and use that lens to separate genuinely differentiated ideas from me-too concepts.

  • Set the innovation guardrails: define what whitespace is genuinely worth chasing, so the pipeline stays focused on the right bets.

  • Manage new product launches end-to-end: lead the NPD process from ideation through consumer insights, concept testing, formulation, plant trials, and packaging development, staying on as the owner of product intent all the way through commercialization and into market. Build a disciplined innovation process and tools covering both stage gate and portfolio management.

  • Shape positioning for new product lines: in partnership with Marketing, define how each new launch sits alongside Seremoni Grade™ and the existing lineup, so the portfolio tells one coherent story.

  • Serve as the central innovation hub and subject matter expert for value-added seafood: track category trends, competitive launches, and retail/foodservice whitespace across seafood and adjacent proteins, translating raw data into recommendations leadership can act on.

  • Build and validate the business case for every innovation project: size the opportunity, model margin and COGS, and run the testing and consumer work needed to de-risk each launch before it scales.


What you’ll own

  • Positioning recommendations for new product lines and brand extensions, in partnership with Marketing

  • Selection of testing partners, co-packers, and vendors for active NPD projects

What you’ll need

  • Ability to translate market insight into sharp product briefs and sales narratives, and to assess risk/reward with imperfect information

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with R&D, supply chain, and sales

  • Strong quantitative fluency: market sizing, COGS optimization, margin modeling, and data analytics

  • Excellent communication across audiences, from R&D technicians to executive leadership

  • Resilience and resourcefulness — this is a startup, and the org chart is still being built


Nice to have

  • Experience with seafood or another animal protein category

  • Familiarity with Jobs-to-Be-Done or similar consumer-insight frameworks
